name: Coronary Sinus Atresia

criteria.description: Absence or atresia of the coronary sinus ostium confirmed by imaging
Retrograde flow in coronary venous system demonstrated by echocardiography or angiography
Identification of alternative venous drainage pathways such as persistent left superior vena cava

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent coronary sinus ostium and retrograde coronary venous flow on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities including echocardiography, cardiac MRI, or angiography.

pathognomonic.notes: Identified via imaging, pathognomonic anatomical feature
Detected by Doppler echocardiography or angiography
searchTerms: backward blood flow in heart veins

common.notes: May occur if associated with other cardiac anomalies
searchTerms: blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

common.notes: Due to impaired cardiac venous drainage
Secondary to arrhythmias from altered cardiac anatomy
Detected on auscultation, may indicate associated defects

occasional.notes: May develop in severe cases or with associated anomalies
Including atrial fibrillation or ventricular tachycardia
Due to transient arrhythmias or reduced cardiac output
Non-specific symptom related to cardiac strain

rare.notes: Due to abnormal venous drainage and stasis
Rare complication due to right-to-left shunting

imaging: Absence of coronary sinus ostium on echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Retrograde coronary venous flow on Doppler studies
Identification of collateral venous pathways such as persistent left superior vena cava on angiography
other: Possible association with other congenital heart defects such as atrial septal defect or persistent left superior vena cava

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of a persistent left superior vena cava draining into the right atrium via the coronary sinus
Presence of a coronary sinus diverticulum rather than atresia

redFlags: Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy
references: Gatzoulis MA, et al. Congenital Heart Disease: Coronary Sinus Atresia. Heart. 2019.
Mavroudis C, Backer CL. Pediatric Cardiac Surgery. 4th ed. 2013.
